children.text: TL;DR

Short answer (October 2026): the best free app to record and transcribe meetings without sending your audio to a vendor is Meetily. It captures Zoom, Google Meet and Microsoft Teams calls from your own computer and transcribes them on the device, so the audio never reaches a cloud server and no bot joins the call. The Community Edition is open source (MIT, 31K+ GitHub stars, 599,000+ downloads) and free without monthly caps, with native Windows and macOS (Apple Silicon) apps.

(opens in new tab)
 is the strongest cloud option on a free plan: unlimited recordings and transcripts, with advanced AI summaries on five calls a month. 
OBS Studio
(opens in new tab)
 is still the most powerful if you can handle the setup. Read on for the full comparison of all 10 tools.

How We Compared These Apps

We compared the same 10 apps on the same criteria and checked every price, free-tier limit and bot or no-bot claim against each vendor's current pricing page, help center or documentation on October 11, 2026. This is a comparison of published plans and documentation, not a lab benchmark: we did not time or score transcription accuracy across tools, so this guide does not rank them on it. Meetily is our product. It is listed first because it fits the criteria below, and we say where another tool is the better fit.
Comparison criteria
Each tool was compared on the same points:
Bot or no bot - Does a recording bot join the call, or does the app capture audio on your own device?
Where audio and transcripts are stored - On your device or in the vendor's cloud?
Offline use - Does recording and transcription work without an internet connection?
Free-tier limits - What the free plan includes: minutes, meetings, AI summaries, retention
Platforms - Windows, macOS, and which meeting apps it works with
Price per user - The paid plan price per user per month, billed annually where the vendor lists it
Setup effort - Judged from each vendor's setup documentation, not timed installs
Our editorial team independently researches and tests products. We may receive referral fees from some links, but this never affects our recommendations.

Why Do Most Meeting Recorders Fall Short?
Before we dive into the options, let's address the elephant in the room. Most meeting recording tools in 2026 fall into one of four traps:
Too complex - Like OBS Studio, which requires configuring virtual audio cables and scene management
Cloud-only audio - Tools that upload your meeting audio to the vendor's servers
Bot-dependent - Tools that join the call as a visible "Notetaker" participant by default. Many now offer a desktop app that records without one, so check which mode the free plan includes
Tight free tiers - Otter's free plan is 300 minutes a month with 30-minute conversations and 3 lifetime imports, and tl;dv's AI notes on the free plan cover only your first 10 meetings
What Makes Good Meeting Recorder Software?

The ideal meeting recording software in 2026 should be simple to set up, work without internet, keep your data local, and never require a visible bot in your meetings. Only a few tools meet all four criteria.
What Is the Best Free Meeting Recorder Software in 2026?
1. Meetily (Best for Local, Open-Source Recording)
Price: Community Edition free (open source, MIT license) | Pro $10/user/month billed annually

Meetily is a meeting recorder that runs on your own computer. Audio is captured and transcribed on your device with no upload step, and the code is public, so you can check that for yourself. The Community Edition is free and has no monthly minute or meeting caps. It is a native Windows and macOS (Apple Silicon) app, and no bot joins the call.
Key Features:
Audio and transcription stay on your device - recordings are never uploaded
AI transcription using Whisper or Parakeet engines, in 99+ languages
Open source (MIT) and self-hosted, so the code can be audited
Free Community Edition with no monthly caps
Native Windows and macOS (Apple Silicon) apps; Linux only by building from the open source repo
Recording and transcription work offline once the models are downloaded
Summaries use a local model or your own API key; if you pick an API provider, only the transcript text is sent to it
No bot in the call - it captures system audio and your microphone
Limitations:
No native CRM integrations
No mobile app yet
Requires local CPU/GPU for transcription
Speaker labels, automatic meeting detection and PDF/DOCX export are Pro features

Best For: Anyone who wants meeting audio and transcripts to stay on their own machine without the setup effort of OBS or an upload to a cloud vendor. Particularly suited for healthcare, legal, and financial teams with compliance requirements.

Advanced AI summaries on the free plan cover the first 5 calls each month; after that you get a general summary template. Fathom joined Superhuman on September 14, 2026, and its announcement says nothing changes for users today.

Best For: Users who want unlimited free recording and are comfortable with a cloud service. Good for individual users who need transcripts but can live with limited AI summaries on the free plan.
3. OBS Studio (Most Powerful, Most Complex)
Price: Free and open source
OBS Studio is the gold standard for screen recording and streaming, but it's overkill for most meeting recording needs.
Key Features:

Supports multiple audio and video sources

Works offline with local storage
Open source (GPLv2 license)

Steep learning curve with complex setup
Virtual audio routing for meetings requires technical knowledge
No built-in transcription or AI features
No meeting-specific features like speaker identification or action items
Best For: Technical users who want maximum control over their recordings and already know OBS, or users who need to record meetings alongside other content (streaming, tutorials).
OBS Setup Warning

If you just want to record meetings, OBS's power becomes a liability. Setting up proper audio routing for a simple Zoom call requires configuring virtual audio cables, scene management, and output settings.
4. Otter.ai (Best for Real-Time Collaboration)
Price: Free (300 min/month) | Pro from $8.33/user/month (annual)

Otter.ai is one of the most well-known AI meeting assistants. Its standout feature is live transcript collaboration, where team members can edit and highlight transcripts in real time during meetings.
Key Features:

Mac and Windows desktop app that records without a bot

Free tier limited to 300 min/month, 30 minutes per conversation, and 3 file imports ever (lifetime)
Audio and transcripts are processed and stored in Otter's cloud
Transcription covers six languages: English, Spanish, French, German, Japanese and Chinese (Mandarin)
No offline capability

Best For: Teams that value real-time transcript collaboration and work in one of its six languages. Teams that need audio to stay off third-party servers will want a local tool instead. See our full Meetily vs Otter.ai comparison for a detailed breakdown.

Fireflies.ai is built for sales teams, with deep CRM integrations that automatically log meeting notes to Salesforce, HubSpot, and Pipedrive. It offers conversation intelligence and sentiment analysis to help improve sales calls.

Best For: Creating async video updates, tutorials, and walkthroughs rather than recording live meetings.

Meetily is not the only local-first option. OpenWhispr

(opens in new tab)

Both are outside the ten tools ranked here, and both release often, so check their current documentation before relying on a specific feature.

children.text: Best Free AI Meeting Recording Software and AI Voice Recorders

If you specifically need AI-powered meeting recording software with transcription and summarization, your options narrow. Not every meeting recorder includes AI features, and the quality varies widely.

AI meeting recording tools use speech-to-text models to automatically transcribe your meetings, identify speakers, and generate summaries with action items. The best AI voice recorders for meetings in 2026 combine accurate transcription with useful post-meeting intelligence.
If you want help across all your meetings rather than one recording at a time, see how Meetily works as an AI meeting assistant. If notes are all you need, the AI note taker page is the shorter read.
Here is how the AI meeting recording software options compare:

Meetily uses OpenAI Whisper and NVIDIA Parakeet models locally, delivering high transcription accuracy on clear English audio. Because transcription runs on your device, meeting audio is not sent to any server. That architecture supports GDPR and HIPAA compliance by design; summaries stay on-device with a local model, or go to the API provider you choose.
Fathom provides cloud-based AI summaries with highlights and video clips. The free plan has unlimited transcription and advanced AI summaries on the first 5 calls each month.
Otter.ai is known for real-time AI transcription during meetings, and transcribes in six languages: English, Spanish, French, German, Japanese and Chinese.
Fireflies.ai adds conversation intelligence and sentiment analysis on top of transcription, a feature-rich option for sales teams. It supports 100+ languages.
tl;dv offers multi-meeting AI reports that analyze patterns across your calls, useful for sales coaching and team reviews. It supports 30+ languages.

OBS Studio does not include AI transcription. The platform-native recorders now add AI notes only through limited free allowances (Zoom's ZoomMate Basic) or paid plans (Google Meet, Teams); see their entries above. If AI transcription is a requirement, choose Meetily or one of the cloud tools listed above.
Why Does Privacy Matter for Meeting Recording?
When you record a meeting, you capture potentially sensitive information:
Business strategies and plans
Client conversations and deal terms
Employee performance discussions
Financial data and projections
Personal details shared in conversation

Cloud-based meeting recording tools store all of this on their servers. Even with encryption, you are trusting a third party with your most sensitive conversations. Model-training policies differ by vendor, so read them. Granola's security page
(opens in new tab)
 says it trains on anonymized data and that you can opt out in Settings, with training off by default for Enterprise workspaces. tl;dv's privacy policy
(opens in new tab)
 says customer content is not used to train AI models.

The risk is not theoretical. In August 2025, a federal class action lawsuit was filed against Otter.ai
(opens in new tab)
 (Brewer v. Otter.ai, N.D. Cal., reported by NPR, August 2025) alleging the bot records meetings and trains on transcripts without all-party consent. In December 2025, Fireflies.ai was sued under Illinois' Biometric Information Privacy Act
(opens in new tab)
 (National Law Review, December 2025) for collecting voiceprints without explicit consent. A local-first recorder like Meetily takes the vendor out of the audio path, because audio and transcription stay on the host's device. Summaries stay local with a local model, or go to the API provider you choose.

Pricing economics push the same way. Cloud speech APIs such as AWS Transcribe
(opens in new tab)
 and Google Cloud Speech-to-Text
(opens in new tab)
 bill per audio minute, and cloud meeting-AI products add their own per-seat plans on top. Self-hosted transcription with OpenAI's open-source Whisper model
(opens in new tab)
 (released under the MIT license in September 2022 by OpenAI) has no per-minute fee.
GDPR and Compliance Warning

For European businesses, sending meeting recordings to a cloud vendor can raise GDPR questions about where the data is processed and under which terms. Otter.ai, Fireflies.ai, and Fathom process meeting audio in the cloud, so review each vendor's data-processing terms and hosting options. Local recording with a tool like Meetily keeps the audio on your own device. See our GDPR compliance guide for more details.
Why Is "OBS Alternative for Meetings" a Top Search?
OBS Studio is powerful, but it wasn't designed as meeting recording software. Here's why people search for OBS alternatives:
Complex setup - Virtual audio routing requires configuring tools like VB-Cable or BlackHole
No transcription - OBS records video and audio, not text
Overkill features - Most users need 5% of what OBS offers
No meeting-specific features - No speaker identification, action items, or AI summaries
Meetily is essentially "OBS for meetings" - all the local, private recording benefits without the complexity, plus AI transcription built in.
How Do I Choose the Right Meeting Recorder Software?
Ask yourself these questions:
Do you need offline capability?

If you travel, work in areas with unreliable internet, or need to record in air-gapped environments, choose Meetily or OBS. All cloud-based tools (Otter, Fireflies, Fathom, tl;dv) require a stable internet connection.
How important is privacy?

If you are recording sensitive business conversations, healthcare discussions, legal meetings, or financial reviews, local-first AI meeting recording tools like Meetily fit best. No cloud provider can leak audio that never left your device.
Do you need a recording bot to be invisible?

If you record client calls, sales demos, or any meeting where a visible "Notetaker" bot would be awkward or unprofessional, choose a tool that captures audio on your own device: Meetily (local, open source) or Granola (cloud processing; the free plan keeps 30 days of history and paid plans start at $14/user/month). Otter.ai, Fireflies, Fathom, and tl;dv join as a visible bot by default; each also has a desktop mode without one (Fathom's is Mac-only), so check that the mode is available on your plan and platform.
Do you need CRM integration?

If your workflow requires meeting notes to automatically sync to Salesforce, HubSpot, or Pipedrive, Fireflies.ai is the strongest option. Meetily has no native CRM integrations; with Meetily Pro, your own script can send notes to a CRM through its webhooks and command-line tool.
Do you need transcription?
If you want searchable, text-based records of your meetings, choose a tool with AI transcription (Meetily, Fathom, Otter, Fireflies, or tl;dv) over basic screen recording (OBS, Loom).
How tech-savvy are you?
OBS requires significant technical knowledge. Every other tool on this list is designed for quick setup, with Meetily and cloud tools ready to record in under 5 minutes.

Conclusion
The best free meeting recorder software in 2026 isn't the one with the most features - it's the one that fits how you actually work.

For people who want audio and transcripts to stay on their own machine, Meetily fits best: local AI transcription, no bot, offline capability, and open source code you can audit. It is what OBS would be if it were designed specifically as meeting recording software.
For unlimited free cloud recording, Fathom stands out with no time caps and no storage limits on its free plan.
For sales teams needing CRM integration, Fireflies.ai is built for it, though a visible bot is the default and its plans have storage limits.
If none of these fits, try Meetily and see whether recording on your own device suits how you work.

children.q: Which meeting apps allow free recording in 2026?
children.a: Three apps allow free meeting recording without a monthly minute cap in 2026: (1) Meetily Community Edition - free, open source under MIT, records and transcribes locally on Windows and macOS with no monthly caps; (2) Fathom Free - unlimited cloud recordings, transcripts and storage (advanced AI summaries on the first 5 calls each month); (3) OBS Studio - free, open source under GPLv2, records anything on screen but requires audio-routing setup and has no transcription. Capped free tiers, checked October 11, 2026: Otter Basic (300 minutes/month, 30 minutes per conversation, 3 lifetime imports), Fireflies Free (400 minutes of storage per seat, 20 one-time AI credits), Granola Free (30 days of meeting history), tl;dv Free (unlimited recordings, but full AI notes only for your first 10 meetings and 5 file uploads, for the life of the account), Loom Starter (25 videos, 5-minute recordings). Zoom's free plan records locally and adds 3 AI summaries a month through ZoomMate Basic.

children.q: How do I record a meeting for free?
children.a: On Windows or macOS, the fastest free path is: (1) Install Meetily Community Edition (free, open source) from meetily.ai; (2) Pick the Whisper or Parakeet transcription engine in setup; (3) Start the recording before joining your Zoom, Google Meet, or Microsoft Teams call. Meetily captures system audio and microphone locally without joining the meeting as a bot, so other participants see no notetaker bot. The recording and transcript stay on your machine, and summaries use a local model or your own API key. If you want a cloud option, Fathom Free records in the cloud and joins as a visible bot unless you use its Mac-only bot-free mode. Our guide on how to record a meeting covers each platform step by step, including consent.

children.q: What's the best free meeting recorder AND transcriber?
children.a: For free recording plus AI transcription in one app, Meetily Community Edition is the strongest pick if you want audio kept on your device: it captures system audio locally (no bot in the call), transcribes with OpenAI Whisper or Parakeet across 99+ languages, and stores everything on-device under the MIT license. Fathom Free is the strongest cloud alternative - unlimited transcription, but audio is processed in Fathom's cloud and its bot-free mode is Mac-only. OBS Studio records audio but does not transcribe. Of the ten tools in this guide, Meetily, OBS Studio and Zoom's local recording keep the recording file on your device, and only Meetily adds on-device transcription. OpenWhispr and Anarlog are other open-source local options outside the ranked list.

children.q: What recording devices work best for in-person meetings?
children.a: For in-person meetings, the recording stack splits into hardware and software. Hardware: a dedicated USB conference mic (Jabra Speak 750, Anker PowerConf S330, or a Blue Yeti) placed centrally on the table captures all speakers cleanly. Phone-based options like an iPhone laid flat work in a pinch. Software: route the mic into a local recorder like Meetily on a laptop and let Whisper transcribe in real time. Meetily works the same way for in-person as for online meetings because it captures whatever audio your system hears. Bot-based cloud tools cannot record an in-person room by joining a call; some offer a separate mobile or desktop app for that, which sends the audio to the vendor's cloud.

children.q: Best meeting recorder and transcriber in 2026?
children.a: The best meeting recorder and transcriber in 2026 depends on whether you need the data to stay local. Best local-first: Meetily - free Community Edition under MIT, no bot, Whisper or Parakeet transcription, works offline. Best cloud free plan: Fathom - unlimited recordings and transcripts, with advanced AI summaries on five calls a month. Best for sales teams: Fireflies.ai with Salesforce/HubSpot CRM sync ($10/user/month billed annually on Pro). Best for Microsoft 365 shops: Microsoft 365 Copilot, an add-on license on top of a qualifying Microsoft 365 plan. Best raw recorder without transcription: OBS Studio.

children.q: What's the best meeting recording app?
children.a: The best meeting recording app for people who want recordings to stay private in 2026 is Meetily: it records Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Discord, and Webex calls locally on Windows or macOS (Apple Silicon), adds no bot to the meeting, and the Community Edition is free under the MIT license. It bundles AI transcription (Whisper or Parakeet) and AI summaries in the same app, so you do not need a separate transcriber. For sales-heavy workflows with CRM dependency, Fireflies.ai is the conventional pick. For unlimited free cloud recording, Fathom is the alternative. None of the other apps in this guide combine bot-free, local, and free in one package.

children.a: Match the app to the constraint. Privacy or compliance constraint (healthcare, legal, financial, regulated industries): Meetily Community Edition - local recording, no audio upload, MIT-licensed. Cost constraint with unlimited free needed: Meetily or Fathom Free. Workflow constraint (CRM sync, sales coaching): Fireflies.ai. Microsoft 365 constraint: Microsoft 365 Copilot inside Teams. Polished notes app: Granola (captures audio on your device without a bot but processes notes in the cloud; the free plan keeps 30 days of history and Business is $14/user/month). For most people who want privacy, low cost, and no bot together, Meetily covers all three.

Our ranked top 10 meeting recording tools for 2026, ordered by the criteria in this guide (where audio is stored first, then bot use and free-tier limits), with primary trade-offs: (1) Meetily - local, no bot, Community Edition free under MIT; (2) Fathom Free - cloud, unlimited free recordings and transcription, bot by default (bot-free on Mac); (3) OBS Studio - powerful local recorder, no transcription, steep setup; (4) Otter.ai - cloud, capped free tier, bot or desktop app, subject of a pending privacy class action; (5) Fireflies.ai - cloud, CRM-friendly, capped free tier, a pending BIPA lawsuit; (6) tl;dv - cloud, free recordings but lifetime-capped AI notes, multi-meeting AI reports; (7) Zoom local recording - Zoom-only, ZoomMate Basic adds 3 summaries a month; (8) Google Meet recording - needs Workspace Business Standard or higher; (9) Microsoft Teams recording - needs a paid Microsoft 365 plan; (10) Loom - async video, free Starter plan limited to 25 videos.

Yes. Meetily's Community Edition is free and open source under the MIT license, with no monthly minute or meeting caps. It includes core features like real-time transcription, AI summaries, and local recording. Pro features like speaker identification, auto-detect meetings, and advanced exports are available at $10/user/month billed annually. The core recorder is free.

children.q: Does Meetily work with Zoom, Teams, and Google Meet?
children.a: Yes, Meetily records any meeting platform because it captures your system audio and microphone. It's platform-agnostic and works with Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, Discord, Slack Huddles, Webex, and any other platform that outputs audio through your computer.

children.q: Can other meeting participants see Meetily recording?
children.a: No bot appears in the call. Meetily is bot-free, which means it doesn't add any visible participant to your meetings. Fireflies, Otter.ai, Fathom and tl;dv join as a visible Notetaker bot by default (each also has a desktop mode that records without one), while Meetily captures audio locally. Only you see that it is recording. You should still follow proper consent laws and inform participants when recording.

All recordings are stored locally on your computer in a folder you choose. Audio is never uploaded to a cloud service. You can back the files up, encrypt them, or delete them anytime. If you use your own API key for summaries, the transcript text is sent to the provider you chose; a local summary model keeps summaries on your device too. This fits GDPR, HIPAA, and other compliance requirements by design, but confirm your own obligations with your compliance team.

children.q: Does Meetily require internet to work?
children.a: No. Once installed and with AI models downloaded, recording and transcription work completely offline. The AI transcription runs on your local machine using Whisper or Parakeet engines. Only the initial download requires internet, and summaries stay offline only with a local model (an API key needs a connection). This suits air-gapped environments and unreliable connections.

Meetily uses OpenAI's Whisper model, which delivers high accuracy on clear audio in English, and supports 99+ languages. The Large v3 model provides the best accuracy, while smaller models (Base, Small) offer faster performance on older hardware.

children.q: What are the system requirements for Meetily?
children.a: Minimum: a Windows PC or an Apple Silicon Mac with 8GB RAM, a 4-core CPU, and 10GB storage. Recommended: 16GB RAM, an 8-core CPU, 50GB storage, GPU acceleration (NVIDIA, AMD, or Apple Silicon), and an SSD. The Whisper Tiny model works on older hardware, while larger models benefit from newer systems.

children.q: Is Meetily GDPR and HIPAA compliant?
children.a: By design, not by certification. Transcription runs on your device, so audio is not sent to a third party, which helps with EU data residency and HIPAA requirements. If you choose your own API key for summaries, that provider receives the transcript text and belongs in your compliance review; a local summary model avoids this. Meetily does not hold formal GDPR or HIPAA certifications, and the open-source code allows security audits. Check your own obligations with your compliance team.

children.q: How can I record a meeting without using Zoom's built-in recorder?
children.a: Use a standalone meeting recorder like Meetily that captures your system audio directly. Install it on your computer, start the recording before your Zoom call, and it will capture everything without using Zoom's native recording. This means no recording notification is sent to participants (though you should still inform them per consent laws), and your recording stays on your local device instead of Zoom's cloud servers.

children.q: Which meeting recorders work for both in-person and online meetings?
children.a: Meetily and OBS Studio both work for in-person meetings because they capture audio from your device's microphone. For in-person meetings, place your laptop in the room and Meetily will record and transcribe using its AI engine. For online meetings, it captures system audio. Cloud tools like Otter.ai and Fireflies join online meetings with a bot by default and offer separate desktop or mobile apps for other situations; their audio goes to the vendor's cloud.

children.q: Are there meeting recorders that don't store audio in the cloud?
children.a: Yes. Meetily stores everything locally on your computer with no audio uploads. OBS Studio also records locally. Zoom offers local recording (not cloud) on its free tier. All other tools in this list - Fathom, Otter.ai, Fireflies.ai, and tl;dv - upload your meeting audio to cloud servers for processing, including in their bot-free desktop modes.
